en: At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks ate almsfood by pressing it down from a mound... [as before] ...
"The training is to be observed: 'I shall not eat almsfood by pressing it down from a mound.
Almsfood is not to be eaten by pressing it down from a mound.
Whoever, out of disrespect, eats almsfood after having pressed it down from a heap, commits an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
There is no offense if it was unintentional.
In the case of one who is absent-minded, one who does not know, or one who is ill.
When only a small amount remains, he gathers it together, crushes it, and eats it;
[this is permissible] in times of distress or for one who is insane.
"For one who is a first offender":
the fifth training rule is concluded.
